common.Control.new: needs project management: the studio serves the one project directory it was launched on (`eda board serve -C dir`) and has no verb to create a new project or document, so there is nothing for New to start
common.Control.open: needs project management: the studio serves one project directory chosen at launch and has no verb to open or switch to another project
common.Control.toggleGridOverrides: needs per-item-type grid overrides (the Edit Grids dialog's connected-items / wires / vias / text / graphics grids and category-aware snapping in the move, drag and route tools); the studio snaps every item to the one grid, so the toggle would switch off nothing. (Ctrl+Shift+G stays bound to Ungroup here; KiCad binds it to this action and leaves Ungroup unbound)
common.Interactive.cycleArcEditMode: needs the arc point editor (PCB_POINT_EDITOR / SCH_POINT_EDITOR arc handles and their three edit modes); the studio's point editor only drags zone corners, so there is no arc edit for the mode to change
common.Interactive.pasteSpecial: nothing to special-case yet: its options are annotation handling for pasted footprints/symbols and clearing the nets of pasted copper, but the studio's clipboard holds no footprints or symbols (only tracks, vias, zones, shapes and text), every copper item must name a net, and the schematic has no copy/paste at all
pcbnew.InteractiveDrawing.placeDesignBlo: needs a design-block library (reusable sub-board blocks); this studio has no block library or block IR
pcbnew.InteractiveDrawing.placeImportedG: needs a DXF/SVG graphics importer; none exists and no new dependencies are allowed
pcbnew.TableEditor.editTable: needs table items (PCB_TABLE); the design IR has no table type
pcbnew.PadTool.explodePad: needs custom-shape pads (a pad made of graphic primitives); the footprint IR models only the six standard pad shapes
pcbnew.PadTool.recombinePad: needs custom-shape pads (a pad made of graphic primitives); the footprint IR models only the six standard pad shapes
pcbnew.MicrowaveTool.createGap: needs a free board footprint: the tool builds a footprint of its own (createBaseFootprint: two rectangular pads, no schematic part) and drops it on the board with doInteractiveItemPlacement, but every board part here comes from the design's schematic and no verb adds one
pcbnew.MicrowaveTool.createStub: needs a free board footprint: the tool builds a footprint of its own (createBaseFootprint: two rectangular pads, no schematic part) and drops it on the board with doInteractiveItemPlacement, but every board part here comes from the design's schematic and no verb adds one
pcbnew.MicrowaveTool.createStubArc: needs a free board footprint (every board part here comes from the design's schematic and no verb adds one) and a custom-shape pad: the arc stub is one PAD_SHAPE::CUSTOM pad with a polygon primitive, and the footprint IR models only the six standard pad shapes
pcbnew.MicrowaveTool.createFunctionShape: needs a free board footprint (every board part here comes from the design's schematic and no verb adds one) and a custom-shape pad: createPolygonShape reads a shape-description file into one PAD_SHAPE::CUSTOM pad, and the footprint IR models only the six standard pad shapes
pcbnew.MicrowaveTool.createLine: needs a free board footprint (every board part here comes from the design's schematic and no verb adds one) and the microwave inductor generator (microwave_inductor.cpp: the S/L meander built from arcs and segments, with its pattern dialog), which nothing here implements
pcbnew.ModuleEditor.createFootprint: needs the footprint wizards, which are Python scripts (FOOTPRINT_WIZARD_FRAME running pcbnew.FootprintWizardBase generators); the studio embeds no Python interpreter
pcbnew.ModuleEditor.checkFootprint: the Footprint Checker is a DRC run (DIALOG_FOOTPRINT_CHECKER over FOOTPRINT_CHECKER); DRC only runs through kicad-cli, which has no footprint-only check, and no DRC engine may be written here -- the board DRC reports the same problems for a placed footprint
eeschema.EditorControl.importGraphics: needs a DXF/SVG graphics importer; none exists and no new dependencies are allowed
eeschema.SymbolDrawing.drawSymbolTextBox: needs text boxes (SCH_TEXTBOX with a border and fill, wrapped text); the library symbol IR has no text box graphic -- only rectangle, polyline, circle, arc and text
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.deriveFrom: needs derived symbols (a symbol that `extends` a parent and inherits its drawing and pins); the library symbol IR has no inheritance, so a derived symbol would have nothing to refer to
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.flattenSym: needs derived symbols: KiCad offers it only for a symbol that extends another (derivedSymbolSelectedCondition) and the library symbol IR has no inheritance (a derived symbol read from a file is flattened on import)
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.updateSymb: needs derived symbols: it re-syncs a symbol with its parent and KiCad itself only answers 'Symbol is not derived from another symbol.' for any other; the library symbol IR has no inheritance, and a handler that always says so would stand in for the missing subsystem
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.showRelate: needs derived symbols: it is offered only for a symbol that extends another or has children (relatedSymbolSelectedCondition), and the library symbol IR has no inheritance
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.showHidden: needs symbol fields on the canvas: the library symbol model keeps no field positions or visibility and the editor draws no fields, so there are no hidden fields to show
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.nextSymbol: belongs to the Symbol Viewer frame (toolbars_symbol_viewer.cpp: a read-only library browser with its own symbol list); the studio has no Symbol Viewer -- the editor's library tree is where symbols are browsed
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.previousSy: belongs to the Symbol Viewer frame (toolbars_symbol_viewer.cpp: a read-only library browser with its own symbol list); the studio has no Symbol Viewer -- the editor's library tree is where symbols are browsed
eeschema.SymbolLibraryControl.exportSymb: plots are kicad-cli's job (`kicad-cli sym export svg`); the studio has no route to it for one symbol and no plotter may be written here
eeschema.InteractiveDrawing.placeDesignB: needs a design-block library (reusable sub-schematic blocks); this studio has no block library or block IR
eeschema.InteractiveEdit.autoplaceFields: needs per-instance symbol field positions (the schematic IR stores no field placement: reference and value are drawn at fixed offsets, so there is nothing to autoplace) and text metrics for the placement search
